In the Indigenous Supports from KHP app, the delta sync process uses change data capture to improve synchronization efficiency on unreliable internet connections. After the initial download, the client sends the timestamp of its last successful synchronization to the .NET API, which then responds only with records created, updated, or deleted since that time instead of transferring the complete dataset. This approach significantly reduces network usage and sync time while ensuring previously synchronized resources remain available offline.

In the Handwritten Digit Classifier project, I chose to use odd values of K because an even value can introduce unpredictable results due to voting ties. I optimized the classifier by training KNN models across these odd values from 1 to 19 and selecting the best K based on validation accuracy.

The Indigenous Supports from KHP app works offline by using a local SQLite database with WatermelonDB for storage, allowing core content and wellness tools to remain available even without an internet connection. When connectivity is available, it employs an incremental delta-sync process based on change data capture to efficiently pull updates from the backend and apply them to the local database, ensuring previously synchronized resources continue functioning smoothly.

I switched from classic RAG to cache-augmented generation because running RAG on my 2-core host took about 32 seconds before the first word appeared, whereas caching my entire knowledge base brought response times down to roughly 5.5 seconds. This performance improvement was critical for Vitae AI, which runs self-hosted on Oracle Cloud's Ampere A1 virtual machine.
